title: Meal Prep Checklist
metaTitle: Meal Prep Checklist for the Week | Gisti
metaDescription: A weekly meal prep checklist: plan, shop, batch-cook, and portion so healthy meals are ready all week. Free, or tailor it to your diet and goals with AI in Gisti.
cardDesc: Plan, shop, batch-cook, and portion — everything to prep a week of meals in one session.
intro: Meal prep saves the two things that derail healthy eating: time and willpower on a busy weeknight. This checklist walks through a single prep session — planning, one shop, batch-cooking, and portioning — so lunches and dinners are ready to grab all week. Use it as-is, or open it in Gisti to tailor it to your diet, and see the rest of our health and fitness checklists.

items.text: Pick 2 to 3 recipes that reheat well
items.note: Stews, grain bowls, roasted veg, and curries hold up far better than salads or crispy foods.

items.text: Plan the week's meals: breakfasts, lunches, dinners, and snacks
Check what you already have in the fridge, freezer, and pantry
Write a shopping list grouped by store section
items.note: Grouping by aisle turns the shop into one fast lap.

items.text: Do a single grocery run for the whole week
Wash and chop all your vegetables at once
Cook grains and starches in bulk: rice, quinoa, pasta, or potatoes
Batch-cook proteins: chicken, ground meat, beans, tofu, or hard-boiled eggs
Roast a big tray of mixed vegetables
Make one sauce or dressing to vary the flavor across meals
items.note: The same base tastes new with pesto one day and a peanut sauce the next.

items.text: Portion meals into containers and label each with the date
Cool food fully before sealing the lids
items.note: Sealing warm food traps steam, goes soggy, and spoils faster.

items.text: Freeze any portions you won't eat within 3 to 4 days
items.note: Cooked meals keep about 3 to 4 days in the fridge; freeze the rest.

items.text: Prep grab-and-go snacks: cut fruit, portioned nuts, or yogurt cups
Arrange the fridge by day or meal so the right container is easy to grab
Clean as you go and wash your containers so next week is easy

faq.q: How long does meal-prepped food last?
faq.a: Most cooked meals keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge in airtight containers. Anything you won't eat in that window should go in the freezer, where most dishes last 2 to 3 months. Always cool food fully before sealing and refrigerating, and label containers with the date.

faq.q: How do I start meal prepping?
faq.a: Start small: prep just lunches, or just one or two dinners, before trying to cook a whole week at once. Pick recipes that reheat well, do one grocery shop, and batch-cook a protein, a grain, and a tray of veg you can mix and match. Build up as the habit sticks.

faq.q: What foods are best for meal prep?
faq.a: Choose foods that reheat without going soggy or mushy: stews, chili, curries, grain bowls, roasted vegetables, cooked grains, and proteins like chicken, beans, and hard-boiled eggs. Store crunchy items, dressings, and fresh greens separately and add them just before eating.
